title: Spectral Bone Density Analysis Lab
description: The user operates a virtual chemistry lab where a prismatic dispersion apparatus is used to project spectral light bands onto a skull specimen for bone density analysis. By adjusting wavelength filters, beam intensity, and incidence angle through interactive controls, the user must calibrate the scattering pattern on the skull to match target diagnostic readings across six spectral zones.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a spectral bone density analysis lab. Load DispersionTest.glb and position it on the left side of the scene as a prismatic light dispersion apparatus. Load ScatteringSkull.glb and place it on the right as the specimen under analysis. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 7) looking at the origin with OrbitControls for navigation. Add a directional light, ambient light, and a colored PointLight between the two models representing the active beam. Create an HTML overlay panel with these interactive controls: (1) a wavelength slider (380nm-780nm) that changes the PointLight color to match the visible spectrum, (2) an intensity slider (0.1-5.0) controlling beam brightness, (3) an incidence angle dial (-45 to 45 degrees) that rotates the DispersionTest model on its Y-axis to aim the beam, (4) a focus distance slider that moves the skull forward/backward along Z, (5) a spectral zone selector with 6 buttons (UV, Violet, Blue, Green, Yellow, Red) each setting a target configuration, and (6) a calibrate button that validates whether current parameters match the selected zone's target values within 5% tolerance. Generate six random but deterministic target configurations on load. When the beam parameters are adjusted, animate particle effects (small THREE.Points) streaming from the dispersion model toward the skull using a ShaderMaterial with color matching the current wavelength. Apply an emissive glow to the skull material that intensifies with beam intensity. Display a real-time readings panel showing current scattering coefficient, absorption index, and density estimate derived from the parameter combination. Track calibration progress with a 6-segment progress bar. When all six zones are successfully calibrated, trigger a completion animation where the skull rotates and all spectral colors cycle through it simultaneously. Ensure all parameter changes animate smoothly with GSAP-style lerping in the render loop.
